items.note: The prompt asks whether to keep using Postgres with pgvector or move to a dedicated vector database.
It gives about 5 million embeddings at 1536 dimensions, adding roughly 1 million per quarter. The ~9M figure for next year follows from that.
It says the data is in Postgres 16 on AWS RDS.
It sets a total budget under $500 per month.
It says every query filters by tenant_id because the system is multi-tenant.
It allows at most 4 options, with pgvector as the baseline.
It asks for a comparison table plus one clear recommendation. It also adds a list of unknowns.
It limits sources to the last 12 months (roughly October 2025 onward).
It asks for a wide scan first, then a deep dive on the top 2.

invented: It says filtered-search performance and recall 'matter as much as unfiltered speed'. The person never ranked these against each other, so this is an added assumption.
